# Ethics of the Citizen

## By the end of today

You will be able to treat voting as a moral act — the delegation of coercive force — and apply reciprocity to that choice.

We began with ethics and force. We end with the citizen who hires that force.

If government derives just power from consent, we are the clients. Government is the hired force.

Jason Brennan: “The symbol of democracy is not just the ballot — it is the ballot connected to a gun.”

Hillel: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor.

Applied to voting: what is hateful to you, do not vote for the government to do to your neighbor.

The right to vote is not the same thing as the rightness of a particular vote.

Texas secession referendum, 1861, is a hard case: a majority voted to protect slavery. Unintended emancipation did not make the intention ethical.

If you vote: understand the thing at its core. Do not outsource that understanding. Vote to protect equal rights — including your own.

## Discussion

1. Is it ever unethical to vote — or unethical *not* to vote?
2. When is a self-interested vote still compatible with equal rights?
3. When, if ever, do you owe more than a ballot?
